_comment: M10 precision-gate baseline (breakwater-quality-policy.md). Real open-source corpus, not synthetic. Regenerate with tools/CorpusScan/run-scan.ps1 and diff against this file before every release (a rise in findings-per-1000-operations needs a reviewed reason, per the quality policy's noise-regression clause).
analyzerCommit: 8d0b568 (M9) + the BW022 fix committed alongside this baseline

sources.name: aspire
sources.note: 5 of 7 candidate Migrations-folder files were CLI-tool migrations unrelated to EF Core (Aspire.Cli project scaffolding), correctly excluded by the MigrationBuilder-body filter

sourcesConsideredButExcluded.name: OrchardCore
sourcesConsideredButExcluded.reason: uses its own YesSql-based IMigration/DataMigration system, not EF Core migrations; 16 candidate files under a 'Migrations' folder, zero contained a MigrationBuilder call

sourcesConsideredButExcluded.name: eShopOnContainers
sourcesConsideredButExcluded.reason: archived predecessor of dotnet/eShop; no Migrations folder found in a shallow clone

approxOperationCountMethod: grep count of migrationBuilder.<Method>( call sites across all copied corpus files -- a proxy for MigrationContext.OperationCount, not the exact analyzer-internal figure (it also counts chained .Annotation(...) calls the analyzer does not count as separate operations), close enough for a noise-regression baseline

byRule.note: 100% legitimate on this sample would also clear the Warning bar, but BW017's Suggestion tier was a deliberate M6 correction (a dropped constraint is often intentional cleanup, not just a noisy-provider concern) documented in breakwater-memory.md, not just a gate artifact -- left as Suggestion

Before the M10 fix this rule counted CreateIndex/AddForeignKey/etc. on a table created earlier in the SAME migration as risky, firing 62 times in this corpus (virtually all on Initial-migration table setup, i.e. an empty table -- a direct violation of breakwater-quality-policy.md principle 4). Fixed in MigrationAnalyzer.BuildContext (src/Breakwater.Analyzers/MigrationAnalyzer.cs): a two-pass scan now excludes tables created in the same Up method from the risky-operation count, the same exemption every other table-lock/data rule already had. Re-scanned after the fix: 13 findings, all on tables that pre-date the migration, all reviewed legitimate. Regression test added: MixedRiskyOperationsRuleTests.Risky_operations_on_a_table_created_in_this_migration_do_not_count_toward_BW022.

rulesWithZeroCorpusFindings.policy: Rules that fire on nothing in the corpus are checked with hand-written cases instead and ship as Warning only if the pattern is unambiguous (breakwater-quality-policy.md).
rulesWithZeroCorpusFindings.verdict: Each of these already has hand-written 'fires' test cases from M4-M9 (tests/Breakwater.Analyzers.Tests/*RuleTests.cs, one file per rule, positive + safe + edge cases per breakwater-test-plan.md) plus a compiling doc example under docs/rules/BW0xx.md verified by DocumentationTests.cs. Those are the hand-written cases the policy calls for; no new hand-written corpus was built separately for M10, since the ones already in the test suite are real, reviewed, and exercised through the actual analyzer (not just described) -- this is a judgment call, see breakwater-memory.md's M10 note for the reasoning and the corpus-size caveat.
rulesWithZeroCorpusFindings.corpusSizeCaveat: 65 real migration files across 4 mid-size open-source repos is a modest sample. Rules whose trigger shape is rare even in a large enough corpus (e.g. BW019 raw-SQL risk patterns, BW031/BW033/BW034's specific dangerous-SQL substrings, BW024 index-on-large-table heuristics) legitimately may not appear here. This baseline does not claim exhaustive real-world coverage; expanding sources.json with more/larger real repos before v0.1.0 would strengthen it further but was not done this session (time-boxed).

artifactsFoundAndFixedDuringThisScan: BW028 initially reported a false positive on every single migration in the corpus (65/65): the scan tool excluded *.Designer.cs (per the analyzer's own 'Down, snapshots and unrelated code are ignored' principle), but a real project's [Migration("id")] attribute lives on the Designer.cs partial of the same class, not the file breakwater itself analyzes. This was a scan-methodology bug, not an analyzer bug: fixed in tools/CorpusScan/run-scan.ps1 by lifting just the attribute text from the Designer.cs sibling onto the copied migration file. Re-scanned: 0 BW028 findings across the whole corpus (correctly silent -- every real migration in this corpus already carries the attribute via its Designer.cs partial).
BW022's true precision bug (table-created-in-this-migration not exempted) -- see the BW022 row above. This one was a genuine analyzer defect, fixed in src/, not a scan-tool artifact.
